Preconditions: Two published templates of the same document type, A and B. A is active.
Steps: Open template B → Publish → Activate. Then reload the gallery.
Expected Result: Exactly ONE template shows as active for that type, and it is B. A is no longer active. Never two, never zero.
Evidence: Doc_template_service::activate() commits one complete assignment
Risk: Two 'official' certificates; a school issues one document believing it issues another

Preconditions: Template A active. Two browser windows, both on template B, both published.
Steps: Click Activate in BOTH windows as close to simultaneously as you can.
Expected Result: Afterwards exactly one template is active for that type. No state where two are active, and none where zero are.
Evidence: activate() single :commit; atomicity under real contention is UNPROVEN
Risk: The failure is silent and legally consequential

Preconditions: A template with a successfully rendered proof.
Steps: Move any block by a visible amount. Do NOT re-proof. Click Publish.
Expected Result: Publish is REFUSED, saying the design changed after the proof was rendered.
Evidence: publish() compares proof.contentHash to contentHash(head)
Risk: A snapshot records a hash no PDF ever produced

Preconditions: A brand-new template, never proofed.
Steps: Attempt to publish, including via the browser console: POST to /doc_templates/publish with only templateId.
Expected Result: Refused by the SERVER, not only by a disabled button. Message names the missing proof.
Evidence: publish() reads lastProof from the head; takes no proof parameter
Risk: A forged proof was possible before 2026-09-02

Preconditions: A template published at least twice (v1 and v2 exist).
Steps: Open version history. Attempt to alter or re-publish v1 by any route the UI offers.
Expected Result: No route exists. v1's content, hash, font manifest and mPDF version are unchanged.
Evidence: publish() refuses an existing version id; no update/delete path on documentTemplateVersions
Risk: 'Show me the template that produced this certificate' becomes unanswerable

Preconditions: Two DIFFERENT users open the SAME template.
Steps: User A edits and waits for autosave. User B then edits and waits for autosave.
Expected Result: User B is told someone else saved it. B's changes are NOT saved and NOT silently merged; A's work is intact.
Evidence: save() lockVersion refusal; client 409 handler keeps the draft dirty
Risk: A statutory template containing text neither person approved

Preconditions: A template open in the designer.
Steps: Disconnect the network. Render a proof. Reconnect. Attempt to publish.
Expected Result: The proof reports FAILURE. Publish remains blocked. At no point does a failed proof appear to have succeeded.
Evidence: api() throws unless r.ok AND parseable AND status!=='error'; E2E U6
Risk: The codebase's standing phantom-success class

Preconditions: Two schools exist. You are signed in to school 1. Obtain a template id belonging to school 2.
Steps: From the console, POST that id to /doc_templates/save, /publish, /activate and /archive in turn.
Expected Result: Every call is refused. School 2's template is unchanged in every respect.
Evidence: Panel uses the Admin SDK and BYPASSES firestore.rules — the check must be in PHP
Risk: Cross-tenant write. Automatic P0 per the ecosystem invariants

Preconditions: An account holding view but not edit or manage.
Steps: Open Certificates. Then POST to /doc_templates/activate from the console.
Input: a valid templateId in your own school
Expected Result: The UI offers no activate control, AND the direct POST is refused by the server with a stated reason.
Evidence: CAPABILITIES map + _remap(); activate requires 'manage'
Risk: Privilege escalation on the act that decides what a school legally issues

Preconditions: An account with no Certificates capability at all.
Steps: Navigate directly to /doc_templates and to /doc_templates/design/<any id>.
Expected Result: Refused/redirected. No template data is visible in the page source or any network response.
Evidence: require_permission() in the constructor; _remap fail-closed

Preconditions: A document type whose ONLY template is currently active.
Steps: Archive that template. Then look at the document-type card for that type.
Expected Result: ⚑ CONTESTED. Candidate A: archiving is refused while the template is the only active one. Candidate B: it is allowed but the school is clearly warned that this type can no longer be issued.
Evidence: archive() clears activeVersion with no sibling check and no warning (02-state-machine T1)
Risk: A school silently loses the ability to issue a statutory document

Preconditions: A template with v4 and v5 published; v5 is active and is wrong.
Steps: Attempt to make v4 active again.
Expected Result: ⚑ CONTESTED. Candidate A: rollback is possible and v4 becomes active. Candidate B: rollback is impossible by design and the UI says so, so the only path is to publish a corrected v6.
Evidence: activate() always uses publishedVersion, never a chosen version (02-state-machine T5)
Risk: A bad publish cannot be undone; the school must republish under pressure

Preconditions: Signed in; the console shows NO '[zxdt] no boot payload' warning.
Steps: Open a starter. Type into a text field. Wait 3 seconds. Reload the page.
Expected Result: The text is still there.
Evidence: markDirty() debounced autosave -> srvSaveDraft() -> POST /doc_templates/save
Risk: THE row. Before this build the designer made zero server calls and nothing was ever saved.

Preconditions: The designer open.
Steps: Open the browser console and read the first lines logged by the page.
Expected Result: No '[zxdt] no boot payload — running OFFLINE' warning. If it IS present, STOP: nothing is being saved and every row below is void.
Evidence: designer.js BOOT/SRV block
Risk: A designer that silently stopped saving looks exactly like one that works

Preconditions: A school with at least one real template.
Steps: Open Certificates and read the template list.
Expected Result: YOUR school's templates are listed. The built-in fixtures 'TC — main letterhead' and 'Bonafide — classic' are NOT shown unless they are genuinely yours.
Evidence: hydrateFromServer() replaces LIB/ACTIVE; empties on failure rather than showing fixtures
Risk: Demo data mistaken for real templates, then activated

Steps: Open a document type → open a classic starter → note the template id shown.
Expected Result: A template is created and its id is a server-minted {schoolId}_TPL#### — not a random 4-digit local placeholder.
Evidence: createOnServer() adopts out.templateId from Doc_template_service::create()
Risk: A client-chosen id could collide with and overwrite an existing template

Preconditions: A complete template.
Steps: Click Proof PDF and wait for it to finish.
Expected Result: It reports a real page count, an engine version and a content hash. The proof unlocks publish.
Evidence: proof_pdf() renders every declared language at p95 and records the proof

Preconditions: A proofed template.
Steps: Publish. Read the dialog. Decline activation. Then activate from the gallery.
Expected Result: The dialog makes clear publishing has NOT changed what prints. Declining changes nothing. Activating changes it, in one step.
Evidence: publishOnServer() then offerActivation(); separate capability grade

Preconditions: A template with at least one published version.
Steps: Open version history.
Expected Result: Every published version lists its proof hash, font manifest and mPDF version.
Evidence: publish() snapshot fields

Preconditions: A template declaring English and Hindi.
Steps: Switch to हिन्दी. Then render a proof and open the produced PDF.
Expected Result: On screen AND in the PDF, Devanagari shows joined conjuncts and correctly placed matras — not boxes, not broken clusters.
Evidence: Doc_renderer useOTL 0xFF, Lohit per script; CON-MULTILINGUAL
Risk: Automated checks prove ink on the page, not that it is READABLE

Preconditions: A PNG school crest on disk.
Steps: Upload it as an image object. Then upload the exact same file again.
Expected Result: It appears both times. The second upload does not create a duplicate stored file.
Evidence: upload_asset() names the file by its own content hash

Preconditions: A .txt file renamed to crest.png.
Steps: Attempt to upload it as an image.
Expected Result: REFUSED, naming the real detected type. Not accepted, not silently ignored.
Evidence: upload_asset(): finfo + getimagesize, extension never trusted
Risk: A .png that is really a script in a web-served directory is an RCE path

Preconditions: An image larger than 4 MB.
Steps: Attempt to upload it.
Expected Result: Refused with a stated size limit.
Evidence: ASSET_MAX_BYTES = 4194304

Preconditions: A template on A5 paper with a long text field.
Steps: Set the sample to p95, fill a field far past its capacity hint, then render a proof.
Expected Result: The proof REFUSES with an overflow error. The text is never silently clipped in the PDF.
Evidence: assertFits()/overflowFindings() measure the real rendered block
Risk: Silent truncation on a legal document

Preconditions: A template with a required merge field bound.
Steps: Render a proof with a sample that cannot resolve that field.
Expected Result: It fails with a named field. A blank is never printed into a statutory field.
Evidence: Doc_serializer throws; CON-FAIL_CLOSED

Preconditions: A proofable template.
Steps: Click 'Render proof' twice in quick succession.
Expected Result: The second click does nothing — the button is disabled while the first runs. Only one proof result is shown, and it is the one you watched.
Evidence: proofOnServer() disables #proofRun for the duration
Risk: Two renders, the later overwriting the earlier's hash

Preconditions: A template with an edit made in the last second.
Steps: Close the tab immediately after typing.
Expected Result: The browser warns before leaving.
Evidence: beforeunload guard while S.dirty
Risk: The debounce window is where the screen is ahead of the server

Preconditions: A template missing a REQUIRED contract field.
Steps: Attempt to publish. Then bypass the UI: POST directly to /doc_templates/publish.
Expected Result: Both refused. The server does not rely on the client's validation.
Evidence: validate() server-side; publish() gates independently
Risk: A constraint enforced only in the client is not enforced

Preconditions: The designer open with unsaved changes.
Steps: Let the session expire (or clear the session cookie), then make an edit and wait for autosave.
Expected Result: The failure is reported to you. It does not appear to save. You are not left believing your work is stored.
Evidence: api() throws on a non-2xx; apiFail() toasts

Preconditions: A school with NO templates for a document type.
Steps: Open that document type.
Expected Result: A clear empty state explaining that a template must be designed, published and activated before anything can be issued. Not a blank page, not a spinner.
Evidence: paintGallery() empty branch

Preconditions: A school with many templates (30+ if you can arrange it).
Steps: Open Certificates and the gallery for the busiest type.
Expected Result: The list renders in reasonable time and remains usable.
Evidence: get_templates() returns all rows for the school with no pagination
Risk: No pagination exists on the template list

Preconditions: The designer open.
Steps: Narrow the window to a laptop width, then to a tablet width.
Expected Result: No horizontal page scroll. Panels and dialogs remain reachable and usable.
Evidence: UX_SPEC; .zxdt is scoped CSS
Risk: The .att-grid collision is the precedent for utility-class leakage

Preconditions: A short viewport (or a laptop in landscape).
Steps: Open the publish dialog and the proof dialog.
Expected Result: Both fit. Content scrolls inside the dialog; the action buttons stay reachable without scrolling the page.
Evidence: Recurring clipping bug class in this codebase

Preconditions: A template with a text object.
Steps: Type a whole word, then press undo ONCE.
Expected Result: The entire typing burst is undone as one entry — not one character per undo.
Evidence: blur pushes one undo entry per burst; input does not

Steps: Read the publish dialog and the activation dialog as if you had never seen this module.
Expected Result: It is unambiguous that publishing freezes a version and activating is what makes it print.
Evidence: UX_SPEC
Risk: The distinction is the module's central concept

Preconditions: A parent account on the Parent app.
Steps: Look for any way to obtain a certificate or document for your child.
Expected Result: There is none, other than raising a Support Desk ticket under 'Certificates & Documents'. Confirms the module does not reach this surface.
Evidence: SupportFirestoreRepository.kt:80,508; no Documents route in NavGraph.kt:122-213
Risk: Documents the pre-issuance baseline

Preconditions: Two schools. A template id belonging to school 2 (ids are {schoolId}_TPL####, numbered from TPL0001).
Steps: From the console POST that id to /doc_templates/save, then /publish, then /activate, then /archive, then /save_block.
Expected Result: All five refused. School 2's template is byte-for-byte unchanged, still active, still published. The refusal message is identical to the one for a NON-EXISTENT id.
Evidence: Doc_template_service::head() tenant check added 2026-09-02; identical-message test
Risk: P0. Was exploitable: activating another school's template changes what they legally issue
Remarks: Re-test of a fixed P0. The identical-message half matters — a different message is an enumeration oracle

Preconditions: A template that has been proofed at least once. Note its id, version and language.
Steps: Sign out entirely (or use a private window). Request https://<host>/uploads/<schoolId>/doctemplates/_proofs/<schoolId>_TPL####_v1_en.pdf
Expected Result: 403 or 404. The PDF does NOT download.
Evidence: uploads/.htaccess denies .pdf; Apache serves static files before CI is reached
Risk: P0. A rendered certificate carries the school's letterhead, crest and signature graphics
Remarks: MUST BE RUN ON THE SERVER, not localhost: it only holds if AllowOverride permits .htaccess. See 07-open-questions Q7

Preconditions: A file you know the path of under another school's uploads directory.
Steps: Set an image object's src to a relative path reaching that file, then render a proof.
Expected Result: The proof is REFUSED with an image-source error. The other school's file is not embedded.
Evidence: Doc_renderer no longer seeds FCPATH.'uploads' as a default image root
Risk: P1. Compounded T0-14 — the embedded file left in a downloadable PDF

Preconditions: An account with Certificates: manage.
Steps: Open the sidebar Certificates menu (Dashboard/Templates/Generate/Issued) and generate one certificate. Then open /doc_templates.
Expected Result: ⚑ CONTESTED. Candidate A: both systems are reachable and that is accepted for now. Candidate B: the legacy generator must be hidden or retired before the new engine is exposed, since one RBAC key grants both.
Evidence: Certificates.php live and sidebar-linked (header.php:662-670); Doc_templates reuses the same key
Risk: P1. The legacy counter is confirmed read-increment-write and mints duplicate numbers under concurrency

Preconditions: The legacy Certificates → Generate screen, and two browsers.
Steps: Generate a certificate in both browsers as close to simultaneously as possible. Compare the two certificate numbers.
Expected Result: ⚑ CONTESTED. Expected by design: they should differ. Expected from the code: they may be IDENTICAL — the counter is a plain RTDB read-then-set whose own comment says 'best-effort atomicity'.
Evidence: Certificates.php:442-450
Risk: P1, pre-existing and outside the new engine — but it is the counter the Issuance Engine must NOT copy
Remarks: Documents the baseline the new engine replaces
